name: field
summary: A form control with its label, description and error wired to it, in that order.

properties.name: label
properties.description: What the control is for, shown above it and its spoken name.

properties.name: hideLabel
properties.description: Hides the label's words; the control keeps it as its name.

properties.name: description
properties.description: Supporting words under the label, read after the name.

properties.name: error
properties.description: What is wrong, shown under the control in the destructive colour; the control is invalid while it has one.

properties.name: required
properties.description: The control must be filled; the label gets a marker and the control's name says required.

properties.name: disabled
properties.description: The control can't be used, and the field fades.

slots.name: control
slots.description: The one control the field names: a text field, a select or any other focusable control.

states.name: rest
states.description: Label, description, control and error in that order, 8 points apart.

accessibility.name: The label names the control, with required when it is; the error, then the description, are the control's help text.
accessibility.keyboard: Adds no tab stop: focus goes to the control, and pressing the label focuses it.
accessibility.web: A <label> for the control, aria-describedby for the description and error, aria-invalid with an error, aria-required with required.
accessibility.apple: The control is named by the label (", required") with the error and description as its hint; the words drawn around it are hidden so nothing is read twice.
accessibility.windows: The control's LabeledBy is the label, HelpText its error then its description, IsRequiredForForm with required; the field adds no element of its own.
accessibility.android: The control's semantics carry the label as its name (", required"), and its error then its description as its state description; the words drawn around it are cleared so nothing is read twice.

cases.person: An Email label with a red marker, the line "We never share it." under it and an empty box.
An Email label, a box with a red edge and the error under it.

deviations: Inside a Form a field with a name shows the form's error for it; native kits have no Form. FieldDescription after the control and Fieldset for a group of controls are web parts.
